title: One folder per research idea, a generated index for each, and a clean repository
request: Review the project and make it clean and structured; add to the README how to run and use everything; create a folder for each separate research idea, from data science to GNNs and whatever comes next; reorganize the whole repository so it reads like a tree or a graph.
spec: research/<track>/ with one shape everywhere (README with the question, prediction contract, status and conclusions; a generated INDEX.md with champion, experiments, notebooks, evaluation, reports and related evidence; experiments/, notebooks/, evaluation/, reports/); planned tracks with their field's leakage traps; a scaffold (make new-track); the root grouped by role (data, research, evidence, shared code); a research map in the Studio; stale and duplicate files removed.
plan: Move loose root files into purpose-named folders and fix every path that depended on them.
Create the research tracks and move each suite with git mv so history is kept; write planned tracks with first experiments and datasets.
Merge the owner's research_tracks/ charters (pushed from another machine) into research/ without losing text.
Group the root by role: data/ (project, public, downloads), evidence/ (campaigns, knowledge), requirements/.
Generate every INDEX.md and the track graph from the registry and the campaigns; keep them fresh in rd-check and CI.
Repair broken data links, remove duplicates and regenerable model binaries, add make clean.
Serve the same track records as a research map in the Studio.

decisions.decision: Keep shared code (dclab_rnd, general_pipeline) at the root.
decisions.why: python -m dclab_rnd and import general_pipeline must work without installation.

decisions.decision: Never move or rename a results/ folder by hand-editing; regenerate the registry after moves.
decisions.why: The registry finds results by path; only path-derived run ids may change.

decisions.decision: Fold overlapping charters into the matching track as sections, and give distinct ones their own track.
decisions.why: The owner asked that nothing be lost, and one idea should live in one place.
About 55 MB of files that experiment scripts write and nothing reads back; their scores stay in the result files.

change: Repository reorganized in several commits: research/ with 22 tracks and a template, scripts/build_research_index.py (later dclab_rnd/research_map.py) generating INDEX.md files and the track graph, data/ and evidence/ grouped by role, requirements/ folder, CLAUDE.md for local sessions, make clean, and a Research map page in the Studio with /api/research.

findings.defect: The ten external-project data symlinks pointed at a folder that no longer existed.
findings.scenario: Each of the ten external projects reached its data through a relative link (../../external_data/<name>). The projects were moved deeper, into research/tabular-classification/ and later into its experiments/ folder, and external_data/ was renamed data/public/, so every link resolved to nothing.
findings.cause: The links were relative paths, and git mv moves a symlink without rewriting its target, so both the deeper location and the renamed target broke them.
findings.fix: Repoint all ten links to data/public/<name>.
findings.impact: Any external-project script or notebook that read its table through the link failed to find it, so none of the ten public projects could be rerun from its own folder.
findings.open: No test checks these links; the link check covered Markdown only, so the next move can break them again without a failing check.

findings.defect: Byte-identical duplicates and a committed run log bloated the repository.
findings.scenario: The model-tagged copy of the LLM review report (Markdown and a 2.8 MB PDF) and its memory, a 'previous' memory archive equal to the gpt-4o-mini snapshot, prototype copies of the v1 SFT samples and two unused benchmark images were all committed twice; plotting code kept re-copying the images.
findings.cause: Copies made for convenience were never removed.
findings.fix: Remove the duplicates and the plotting code that re-copied them; scripts/clean_workspace.py removes caches and empty folders without touching tracked files, data, environments or secrets.
findings.impact: Every clone carried a second 2.8 MB PDF and copies that could drift from their originals, and the plotting code would have recreated the image copies on its next run.

measurements.name: registry and links after the moves
measurements.gate: A move may change paths, path-derived run ids and timestamps, never a number or a finding; every Markdown link must resolve.
measurements.result: Same 579 registry records with identical metrics; regenerated files differed only in paths, path-derived run ids and one timestamp; all relative Markdown links resolve; checks passed locally and in a clean CI-only environment.
measurements.next: Keep make research-index in rd-check so an INDEX never goes stale.
measurements.against_gate: The registry kept the same 579 records with identical metrics, the regenerated files differed only in paths, path-derived run ids and one timestamp, and every relative Markdown link resolves: each condition of the gate holds.
limits: Markdown links were checked; symlinks were not, and the broken data links were found by hand.
A diff of generated files proves nothing was lost only for generated files; hand-written documents rely on the link check alone.

outcome: 22 research tracks with one shape and a generated index each, a root grouped by role, a research map in the app, and CLAUDE.md so later local sessions start with the map, commands and rules.
lessons: Move with git mv and regenerate every derived file, then diff the generated files: only paths should change.
A reorganization must check links that git does not track semantically (symlinks, notebook data paths, script root depths).
risks: Moving a results/ folder so the registry no longer finds it, or changing a number on the way.
Symlinks and relative paths that git mv does not rewrite.
Losing text when merging the owner's track charters from another machine.
Moving shared code into a folder where python -m dclab_rnd stops working without installation.
Generated INDEX files going stale after the moves.
